TASK.TEXT: Long ago, a young sailor named Mira found
an old map tucked inside a bottle that had
washed up on the beach. Its ink was faded,
but she could still make out a reef, a bay
and a big red cross near a sunken tower.
She traded her fishing nets for a used
diving suit, a brass helmet and a long air
hose. Her friend Tomas, who owned a small
boat, agreed to help in return for a share
of whatever treasure they might discover.
They set out at sunrise. The water was calm
and blue, and dolphins raced along beside
the bow. By noon they reached the reef from
the map, a ring of coral that glowed gold
and green just below the rippling surface.
Mira climbed down the ladder and sank into
the cool water. Fish of every color swirled
around her. Far below she spotted the old
tower, leaning in the sand and wrapped in
long ribbons of swaying green seaweed.
Then a shadow passed overhead. A grey shark
circled slowly, watching her with flat dark
eyes. Mira stayed perfectly still, holding
her breath, until the shark lost interest
and drifted away toward deeper water.
Inside the tower she found a rusty iron box
half buried in the sand. She tugged on its
handle and it came free with a puff of silt.
She tied the box to her rope and gave three
sharp pulls, the signal to bring her up.
Back on deck, Tomas pried open the lid. It
held no gold at all, only a second map and
a note that read: the real prize lies much
deeper. Mira laughed, wrung out her hair and
said they would set sail again tomorrow.
